nodes.name: Every 10 min, 23:00-04:00
nodes.notes: n8n's GENERIC_TIMEZONE is Asia/Riyadh, so this is 23:00-03:59 LOCAL = 20:00-00:59 UTC. DeepSeek's peak is 01:00-04:00 and 06:00-10:00 UTC Mon-Fri, where every rate doubles; this window is entirely outside both, which halves the judge bill for the same work. It must also FINISH before 04:00 local (01:00 UTC), which is why the window ends at 03:59 rather than running to dawn.

parameters.query:
-- lease-exempt: this is REGISTRATION, before any lease exists. It writes
-- only chat_eval_jobs' own queue columns and never touches claim_token,
-- claim_until or a row in flight -- the ON CONFLICT clause reopens only
-- 'evaluated' and 'unscoreable', both of which are unleased by definition.
--
-- Register every thread the idle rule says is finished.
--
-- THE RULE IS NOT HERE. `v_chat_eval_due` owns "silent for 3 days (2 until
-- 017), has both sides, at least 2 messages". A copy of that predicate in this
-- node would be a second definition to keep in step with the backfill's.
--
-- ALREADY-ANALYSED THREADS ARE REGISTERED AS 'evaluated', not skipped, so the
-- ON CONFLICT below can still reopen them if they grow.
--
-- REOPENING, AND ITS CEILING (017). A thread that gains messages after being
-- judged is judged again against the fuller thread -- a score computed over
-- half a conversation is worse than a late one. That rule had no limit, and
-- the judge bill is the only cost in this system that scales without one, so
-- two conditions now bound it:
--
--   judge_runs < 2                       at most one re-judge, ever.
--   observed >= judged * 1.5             and only if the thread grew by half.
--
-- Why not "any new message": one "شكرا" arriving three days later moves no
-- module score, and re-judging for it pays full price for the same answer.
--
-- Only 'evaluated' and 'unscoreable' reopen: 'dead_letter' is a decision a
-- human made and must not be undone by traffic, and 'evaluating' /
-- 'judge_failed' / 'pending' are already in flight.
INSERT INTO chat_eval_jobs (interaction_id, idle_through, status, observed_message_count)
SELECT d.interaction_id,
       d.last_message_at,
       CASE WHEN a.interaction_id IS NOT NULL THEN 'evaluated' ELSE 'pending' END,
       d.message_count
FROM v_chat_eval_due d
LEFT JOIN interaction_analysis a ON a.interaction_id = d.interaction_id
ON CONFLICT (interaction_id) DO UPDATE SET
  status = CASE
    WHEN EXCLUDED.idle_through > chat_eval_jobs.idle_through
         AND chat_eval_jobs.status IN ('evaluated', 'unscoreable')
         AND chat_eval_jobs.judge_runs < 2
         AND EXCLUDED.observed_message_count
             >= coalesce(chat_eval_jobs.judged_message_count, 0) * 1.5
      THEN 'pending'
    ELSE chat_eval_jobs.status
  END,
  -- Attempts belong to the version of the thread they were spent on. A
  -- reopened thread is a new piece of work and starts with a full budget.
  judge_attempts = CASE
    WHEN EXCLUDED.idle_through > chat_eval_jobs.idle_through
         AND chat_eval_jobs.status IN ('evaluated', 'unscoreable')
         AND chat_eval_jobs.judge_runs < 2
         AND EXCLUDED.observed_message_count
             >= coalesce(chat_eval_jobs.judged_message_count, 0) * 1.5
      THEN 0 ELSE chat_eval_jobs.judge_attempts
  END,
  next_attempt_at = CASE
    WHEN EXCLUDED.idle_through > chat_eval_jobs.idle_through
         AND chat_eval_jobs.status IN ('evaluated', 'unscoreable')
         AND chat_eval_jobs.judge_runs < 2
         AND EXCLUDED.observed_message_count
             >= coalesce(chat_eval_jobs.judged_message_count, 0) * 1.5
      THEN now() ELSE chat_eval_jobs.next_attempt_at
  END,
  idle_through = GREATEST(chat_eval_jobs.idle_through, EXCLUDED.idle_through),
  -- Always refreshed, reopen or not: it is the yardstick the +50% test uses
  -- next time, and a stale one would let a thread reopen on growth it already
  -- had.
  observed_message_count = EXCLUDED.observed_message_count,
  updated_at = now()
RETURNING interaction_id, status;

-- lease-exempt: this IS the lease breaker. Matching on claim_token would
-- defeat its only purpose, which is to reclaim rows from workers that are
-- gone. It is safe because it only touches rows whose claim_until has
-- already passed, and it clears the token as it goes.
-- Give back the work of executions that died holding a lease.
--
-- 'transcribing' and 'evaluating' mean "a worker holds this row right now".
-- If the worker crashed, was cancelled, or hung past claim_until, nothing else
-- would ever pick the row up again: it is not 'discovered', not failed, and
-- not terminal, so no claim predicate matches it. That is a permanent loss of
-- exactly the kind 008 exists to prevent, and it is invisible -- the row looks
-- busy forever.
--
-- Recovery puts the row back in the stage-appropriate failed state so the
-- normal retry budget applies, and only dead-letters it once that budget is
-- spent. The cooldown is the same 45 minutes the failure paths use: a run that
-- died because the ASR Space was throttling must not be re-claimed instantly.
--
-- The attempt was already counted at claim time, so recovery does not count it
-- again -- that is the whole point of counting at claim: a worker that dies
-- without writing anything still spent an attempt, and a poison row cannot be
-- claimed forever.
--
-- $1 = cooldown minutes, $2 = max attempts per stage.
--
-- A worker that died mid-judge leaves a job 'evaluating' with a lease nobody
-- will ever release. Reclaim it once the lease is provably dead.
--
-- ATTEMPTS WERE ALREADY SPENT at claim time, so a crash loop cannot run
-- forever: three expiries and the job is dead-lettered and visible, rather
-- than retried silently until the judge budget is gone.
UPDATE chat_eval_jobs
   SET status = CASE WHEN judge_attempts >= 3 THEN 'dead_letter' ELSE 'judge_failed' END,
       claim_token     = NULL,
       claim_until     = NULL,
       claimed_at      = NULL,
       -- Back off further each time. A judge that is down stays down for
       -- minutes, and hammering it is how a rate limit becomes a ban.
       next_attempt_at = now() + (interval '5 minutes' * GREATEST(judge_attempts, 1)),
       last_error      = 'lease expired after ' || judge_attempts
                         || ' attempt(s): worker vanished mid-judge',
       updated_at      = now()
 WHERE status = 'evaluating'
   AND claim_until < now()
RETURNING interaction_id, status;

nodes.name: Claim work

parameters.query:
-- Take exactly one job, and make the taking visible to every other runner.
--
-- SKIP LOCKED, not a plain FOR UPDATE: two overlapping ticks must take
-- different rows, never queue behind the same one. LIMIT 1 keeps a slow judge
-- from holding a batch of leases it cannot finish inside them.
--
-- ATTEMPTS ARE INCREMENTED AT CLAIM TIME, not on failure. A worker that dies
-- before it can record anything has still spent an attempt, and that is the
-- only version of this counter that a crash cannot reset.
--
-- OLDEST IDLE FIRST: the thread that has been waiting longest is the one whose
-- coaching is most overdue.
WITH pick AS (
  SELECT j.interaction_id
  FROM chat_eval_jobs j
  WHERE j.status IN ('pending', 'judge_failed')
    AND j.next_attempt_at <= now()
  ORDER BY j.idle_through
  -- 017: was LIMIT 1, a hard ceiling of 48 evaluations a day at one
  -- tick per 30 minutes. Ten per tick across the nightly window is ~300 a
  -- night, which clears 200 chats/day with headroom. Raise this and the
  -- HTTP batching on "Two AI passes" has to move with it.
  LIMIT 10
  FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED
)
UPDATE chat_eval_jobs j
   SET status         = 'evaluating',
       claim_token    = gen_random_uuid(),
       claimed_at     = now(),
       -- Longer than the judge's own 300 s timeout plus both passes, so a slow
       -- but healthy run is never reclaimed underneath itself.
       claim_until    = now() + interval '15 minutes',
       judge_attempts = j.judge_attempts + 1,
       last_error     = NULL,
       updated_at     = now()
  FROM pick
 WHERE j.interaction_id = pick.interaction_id
RETURNING j.interaction_id::text AS interaction_id,
          j.claim_token::text    AS claim_token,
          j.judge_attempts;

nodes.notes: Returns nothing when there is no work, which ends the execution here. That is the intended idle path -- no IF node required.

parameters.query:
-- The thread as the judge must read it: every message, in the order it was
-- sent.
--
-- ORDERED BY sent_at, NOT seq. 01c renumbers seq after every batch, and a
-- thread read mid-renumber must still come out in the order the messages were
-- actually sent. seq is the tie-break only.
--
-- TIMESTAMPS RENDERED EXPLICITLY IN UTC WITH THE OFFSET SPELLED OUT.
-- to_jsonb() on a timestamptz renders it in the session TimeZone, which n8n
-- does not set, so the same row could be handed to the worker as +03 today and
-- +00 tomorrow. after_hours converts before comparing (gotcha 11), which it
-- can only do if the offset actually arrives.
SELECT i.interaction_id::text AS interaction_id,
       i.external_id,
       i.channel::text        AS channel,
       coalesce(jsonb_agg(
         jsonb_build_object(
           'seq',     m.seq,
           'sender',  m.sender::text,
           'body',    m.body,
           'sent_at', to_char(m.sent_at AT TIME ZONE 'UTC',
                              'YYYY-MM-DD"T"HH24:MI:SS') || '+00:00'
         ) ORDER BY m.sent_at, m.seq
       ) FILTER (WHERE m.message_id IS NOT NULL), '[]'::jsonb) AS messages
FROM interactions i
LEFT JOIN chat_messages m ON m.interaction_id = i.interaction_id
WHERE i.interaction_id = $1::uuid
GROUP BY i.interaction_id, i.external_id, i.channel;

parameters.query:
-- Pass 1 is stored on its own merit: a good customer extraction naming a hot
-- lead survives a pass-2 failure, because it is the half that drives revenue.
--
-- FENCED. `r` selects FROM lease, so an execution whose lease was reclaimed
-- writes nothing and returns nothing, and 'Pass 1 stored?' stops the chain.
-- The lease is a real row lock (FOR UPDATE) on a LIVE claim, not an unlocked
-- existence check: an unlocked check reads a snapshot and then lets go, and
-- the recovery sweep can reclaim the row inside that window while this write
-- still commits.
--
-- input_type IS 'chat'. It is what makes a chat score comparable only with
-- other chat scores -- v_quality_by_input groups on it, and a chat averaged
-- together with call transcripts compares typed text against 0.6-confidence
-- ASR output.
--
-- ON CONFLICT REFRESHES EVERY VALUE DERIVED FROM THIS RESPONSE, including
-- prompt_version and model. A re-judged thread whose provenance still names
-- the previous run is what makes a prompt A/B unreadable six weeks later.

WITH lease AS MATERIALIZED (
  SELECT j.interaction_id
  FROM chat_eval_jobs j
  WHERE j.interaction_id = $3::uuid
    AND j.claim_token    = $4::uuid
    AND j.status         = 'evaluating'
    AND j.claim_until    > now()
  FOR UPDATE
),
r AS (SELECT $2::jsonb AS d FROM lease),
p AS (
  SELECT coalesce(d->'pass1'->'payload', '{}'::jsonb)
         || jsonb_build_object('pass1_validation',
              coalesce(d->'pass1'->'payload'->'pass1_validation',
                       d->'pass1'->'pass1_validation',
                       '{}'::jsonb)) AS payload,
         d
  FROM r
)
INSERT INTO interaction_analysis (
  interaction_id, schema_version, prompt_version, model, input_type,
  source_quality, language, intent, summary_ar, confidence,
  uncertain_fields, raw_response
)
SELECT
  $1::uuid,
  '1.0',
  p.d->'pass1'->>'prompt_version',
  p.d->'pass1'->>'model',
  'chat'::input_type,
  -- 1.00, and not by default: a chat is the customer's own typed words, with
  -- no transcription step to lose or invent a digit. The column exists to let
  -- a forecast weight a budget read off a 0.60-confidence transcript below one
  -- the customer typed, and this is the case it is measuring against.
  1.00,
  left(p.payload->>'language', 2),
  p.payload->>'intent',
  p.payload->>'summary_ar',
  (p.payload->>'confidence')::numeric,
  coalesce(p.payload->'uncertain_fields', '[]'::jsonb),
  p.payload
FROM p
ON CONFLICT (interaction_id) DO UPDATE SET
  schema_version   = EXCLUDED.schema_version,
  prompt_version   = EXCLUDED.prompt_version,
  model            = EXCLUDED.model,
  input_type       = EXCLUDED.input_type,
  source_quality   = EXCLUDED.source_quality,
  language         = EXCLUDED.language,
  intent           = EXCLUDED.intent,
  summary_ar       = EXCLUDED.summary_ar,
  confidence       = EXCLUDED.confidence,
  uncertain_fields = EXCLUDED.uncertain_fields,
  raw_response     = EXCLUDED.raw_response,
  updated_at       = now()
RETURNING interaction_id::text AS interaction_id;

options.queryReplacement: ={{ [ $('Claim work').item.json.interaction_id, JSON.stringify($('Two AI passes').item.json), $('Claim work').item.json.interaction_id, $('Claim work').item.json.claim_token ] }}

parameters.query:
-- Pass 2, with status as first-class columns (014).
--
-- FENCED, like every durable write here.
--
-- WHICH STATUSES REACH THIS NODE: 'ok' and 'ungradeable'. Both are stored --
-- ungradeable is terminal data quality, and a row recording why there is no
-- number is what keeps it out of a denominator instead of hidden from every
-- report. 'unscoreable' never gets here (it is refused before pass 1 and has
-- its own node), and 'contract_failed' is routed to 'Mark judge failed',
-- which retries.
--
-- gradeable IS AND-ed WITH "a score arrived". A response claiming gradeable
-- with a null score is self-contradictory, and storing it that way creates a
-- state no view has a bucket for.

WITH lease AS MATERIALIZED (
  SELECT j.interaction_id
  FROM chat_eval_jobs j
  WHERE j.interaction_id = $3::uuid
    AND j.claim_token    = $4::uuid
    AND j.status         = 'evaluating'
    AND j.claim_until    > now()
  FOR UPDATE
),
r AS (SELECT $2::jsonb AS d FROM lease)
INSERT INTO agent_evaluations (
  interaction_id, agent_id, schema_version, prompt_version, rubric_version, model,
  input_type, source_quality, final_score, performance_level, weight_applied,
  m1_reception, m2_offer, m3_objections, m4_followup, m5_closing,
  breakdown, evidence, stage_reached, behavior_flags,
  contract_status, gradeable, ungradeable_modules, evidence_rejected,
  model_fingerprint, top_strength, top_weakness, top_recommendation, notes,
  raw_response
)
SELECT $1::uuid, i.agent_id, '1.0',
  d->'pass2'->>'prompt_version', d->>'rubric_version', d->'pass2'->>'model',
  'chat'::input_type,
  1.00,
  (d->'pass2'->>'final_score')::numeric,
  d->'pass2'->>'performance_level',
  (d->'pass2'->>'weight_applied')::numeric,
  (d->'pass2'->'modules'->>'module1_reception')::numeric,
  (d->'pass2'->'modules'->>'module2_offer')::numeric,
  (d->'pass2'->'modules'->>'module3_objections')::numeric,
  (d->'pass2'->'modules'->>'module4_followup')::numeric,
  (d->'pass2'->'modules'->>'module5_closing')::numeric,
  coalesce(d->'pass2'->'payload'->'modules', '{}'::jsonb),
  coalesce(d->'pass2'->'payload'->'evidence', '[]'::jsonb),
  nullif(d->'pass2'->'payload'->>'stage_reached', '')::conversation_stage,
  coalesce(d->'pass2'->'payload'->'behavior_flags', '[]'::jsonb),
  coalesce(nullif(d->'pass2'->>'contract_status', ''), 'ok'),
  coalesce((d->'pass2'->>'gradeable')::boolean, true)
    AND (d->'pass2'->>'final_score') IS NOT NULL,
  CASE WHEN jsonb_typeof(d->'pass2'->'ungradeable_modules') = 'array'
       THEN d->'pass2'->'ungradeable_modules' ELSE '[]'::jsonb END,
  CASE WHEN jsonb_typeof(d->'pass2'->'evidence_rejected') = 'array'
       THEN d->'pass2'->'evidence_rejected' ELSE '[]'::jsonb END,
  nullif(coalesce(d->'pass2'->'usage'->>'system_fingerprint',
                  d->'pass2'->>'system_fingerprint',
                  d->'pass2'->>'model_fingerprint'), ''),
  d->'pass2'->'payload'->'summary'->>'top_strength',
  d->'pass2'->'payload'->'summary'->>'top_weakness',
  d->'pass2'->'payload'->'summary'->>'top_recommendation',
  d->'pass2'->'payload'->>'notes',
  d->'pass2'->'payload'
FROM interactions i, r
WHERE i.interaction_id = $1::uuid
ON CONFLICT (interaction_id) DO UPDATE SET
  agent_id            = EXCLUDED.agent_id,
  schema_version      = EXCLUDED.schema_version,
  prompt_version      = EXCLUDED.prompt_version,
  rubric_version      = EXCLUDED.rubric_version,
  model               = EXCLUDED.model,
  input_type          = EXCLUDED.input_type,
  source_quality      = EXCLUDED.source_quality,
  final_score         = EXCLUDED.final_score,
  performance_level   = EXCLUDED.performance_level,
  weight_applied      = EXCLUDED.weight_applied,
  m1_reception        = EXCLUDED.m1_reception,
  m2_offer            = EXCLUDED.m2_offer,
  m3_objections       = EXCLUDED.m3_objections,
  m4_followup         = EXCLUDED.m4_followup,
  m5_closing          = EXCLUDED.m5_closing,
  breakdown           = EXCLUDED.breakdown,
  evidence            = EXCLUDED.evidence,
  stage_reached       = EXCLUDED.stage_reached,
  behavior_flags      = EXCLUDED.behavior_flags,
  contract_status     = EXCLUDED.contract_status,
  gradeable           = EXCLUDED.gradeable,
  ungradeable_modules = EXCLUDED.ungradeable_modules,
  evidence_rejected   = EXCLUDED.evidence_rejected,
  model_fingerprint   = EXCLUDED.model_fingerprint,
  top_strength        = EXCLUDED.top_strength,
  top_weakness        = EXCLUDED.top_weakness,
  top_recommendation  = EXCLUDED.top_recommendation,
  notes               = EXCLUDED.notes,
  raw_response        = EXCLUDED.raw_response,
  updated_at          = now()
RETURNING interaction_id::text AS interaction_id;

nodes.name: Assess deal

parameters.query:
-- Assess the DEAL from the conversation that was just analysed.
--
-- WHY THIS EXISTS. The CRM stage is set by hand by the agent who owns the
-- deal, and the agent who forgets to move a deal to 'lost' is the same agent
-- whose conversations we are grading. So the outcome is read from what the
-- customer actually said instead. stage_id and amount are NOT touched: the
-- two disagreeing is the finding, and overwriting the CRM's answer with ours
-- would destroy the comparison this whole column family exists to make.
--
-- THE MODEL DOES NOT DECIDE THE OUTCOME. deal_outcome_from_analysis() (015)
-- maps the two things pass 1 can observe -- is_real_inquiry and buying_stage --
-- onto won/lost/in_progress/no_opportunity/unknown by a fixed rule. Asking a
-- model "did this deal close" gets a confident answer from a conversation that
-- does not support one.
--
-- CREATING THE ROW IS NOT THE STUB THE INGEST RULE FORBIDS. Ingest must never
-- invent a deal, because a deal with no stage, no amount and no owner pollutes
-- every funnel report. This row is different in the two ways that matter: the
-- id is the real Bitrix deal id the API sent, and origin = 'ai_derived' says
-- exactly where it came from, so no report can mistake it for a CRM record.
--
-- LATEST CONVERSATION WINS. A deal can have many conversations, and only the
-- most recent one's outcome is current. The guard compares CONVERSATION time
-- (ai_conversation_at), not assessment time: re-judging an old thread today
-- must not overwrite the outcome read from a newer one last week.

WITH lease AS MATERIALIZED (
  SELECT j.interaction_id
  FROM chat_eval_jobs j
  WHERE j.interaction_id = $3::uuid
    AND j.claim_token    = $4::uuid
    AND j.status         = 'evaluating'
    AND j.claim_until    > now()
  FOR UPDATE
),
src AS (
  SELECT i.external_deal_id                              AS bitrix_deal_id,
         i.interaction_id,
         coalesce(i.ended_at, i.started_at)              AS conversation_at,
         a.raw_response,
         a.prompt_version,
         a.model,
         a.confidence
  FROM lease
  JOIN interactions i          ON i.interaction_id = lease.interaction_id
  JOIN interaction_analysis a  ON a.interaction_id = i.interaction_id
  WHERE i.external_deal_id IS NOT NULL
    AND i.external_deal_id <> ''
)
INSERT INTO deals (
  bitrix_deal_id, origin, service, lead_temp,
  ai_outcome, ai_outcome_reason, ai_stage_reached, ai_service, ai_lead_temp,
  ai_budget_amount, ai_currency, ai_confidence,
  ai_assessed_at, ai_conversation_at, ai_assessed_from,
  ai_prompt_version, ai_model
)
SELECT
  src.bitrix_deal_id,
  'ai_derived',
  -- The non-ai columns are seeded once on INSERT so a brand-new row is not
  -- entirely null, and never touched again by this workflow: if the CRM import
  -- later fills them, that is the authoritative answer and this must not
  -- overwrite it.
  coalesce(nullif(src.raw_response->'trip'->>'service', ''), 'unknown')::service_type,
  coalesce(nullif(src.raw_response->'commercial'->>'lead_temperature', ''), 'unknown')::lead_temperature,
  deal_outcome_from_analysis(src.raw_response),
  left(coalesce(src.raw_response->>'summary_ar', ''), 500),
  src.raw_response->'commercial'->>'buying_stage',
  coalesce(nullif(src.raw_response->'trip'->>'service', ''), 'unknown')::service_type,
  coalesce(nullif(src.raw_response->'commercial'->>'lead_temperature', ''), 'unknown')::lead_temperature,
  (src.raw_response->'commercial'->>'budget_amount')::numeric,
  left(nullif(src.raw_response->'commercial'->>'budget_currency', ''), 3),
  src.confidence,
  now(),
  src.conversation_at,
  src.interaction_id,
  src.prompt_version,
  src.model
FROM src
ON CONFLICT (bitrix_deal_id) DO UPDATE SET
  ai_outcome         = EXCLUDED.ai_outcome,
  ai_outcome_reason  = EXCLUDED.ai_outcome_reason,
  ai_stage_reached   = EXCLUDED.ai_stage_reached,
  ai_service         = EXCLUDED.ai_service,
  ai_lead_temp       = EXCLUDED.ai_lead_temp,
  ai_budget_amount   = EXCLUDED.ai_budget_amount,
  ai_currency        = EXCLUDED.ai_currency,
  ai_confidence      = EXCLUDED.ai_confidence,
  ai_assessed_at     = EXCLUDED.ai_assessed_at,
  ai_conversation_at = EXCLUDED.ai_conversation_at,
  ai_assessed_from   = EXCLUDED.ai_assessed_from,
  ai_prompt_version  = EXCLUDED.ai_prompt_version,
  ai_model           = EXCLUDED.ai_model,
  updated_at         = now()
WHERE deals.ai_conversation_at IS NULL
   OR EXCLUDED.ai_conversation_at >= deals.ai_conversation_at
RETURNING bitrix_deal_id, ai_outcome, origin;

nodes.notes: Reads the pass-1 row just written rather than the HTTP response, so the assessment can only ever describe an analysis that is actually stored. Outputs nothing when the thread carries no deal id, which is not a failure.

parameters.query:
-- fence-exempt: single-statement UPDATE. The fence IS the statement's own
-- WHERE clause, so the row is locked and the predicate re-evaluated against
-- the latest committed version by the UPDATE itself (EvalPlanQual). There is
-- no read-then-write window to widen, and adding FOR UPDATE would only take
-- the same lock twice.
-- Terminal success. The lease is released and last_error cleared, so a row that
-- previously failed does not keep a stale reason attached to a good result.
--
-- Terminal, and the happy path. Fenced: a job whose lease was reclaimed while
-- the judge was running must not be marked done by the execution that lost it.
--
-- 017: judge_runs is the ceiling the reopen rule reads, and
-- judged_message_count is the yardstick its +50% test measures from. Both are
-- written HERE, at the only point a judge is known to have completed -- setting
-- them at claim time would count an attempt that died mid-call as a run.
UPDATE chat_eval_jobs
   SET status      = 'evaluated',
       claim_token = NULL,
       claim_until = NULL,
       claimed_at  = NULL,
       last_error  = NULL,
       judge_runs  = judge_runs + 1,
       judged_message_count = coalesce(observed_message_count, judged_message_count),
       updated_at  = now()
 WHERE interaction_id = $1::uuid
   AND claim_token    = $2::uuid
   AND status         = 'evaluating'
RETURNING interaction_id, status, judge_attempts, judge_runs;

-- fence-exempt: single-statement UPDATE. The fence IS the statement's own
-- WHERE clause, so the row is locked and the predicate re-evaluated against
-- the latest committed version by the UPDATE itself (EvalPlanQual). There is
-- no read-then-write window to widen, and adding FOR UPDATE would only take
-- the same lock twice.
-- Terminal success. The lease is released and last_error cleared, so a row that
-- previously failed does not keep a stale reason attached to a good result.
--
-- Terminal, and NOT a failure. Three different kinds of nothing arrive here:
-- a bot-only thread with no agent to grade, a thread where every turn is
-- labelled as the agent (a source labelling fault, not a conversation), and a
-- thread holding less text than the scoring minimum.
--
-- Retrying any of them re-asks a model that already answered, or asks one
-- about a conversation that is not there, and can only manufacture a score. So
-- the reason is written down and the job stops.
--
-- NO agent_evaluations ROW IS WRITTEN. Workflow 02 does write one for an
-- unscoreable call, because a call that was recorded and could not be
-- transcribed is a quality signal about the ASR. These are different: there is
-- no agent turn to grade at all, and a row under an agent's name for a thread
-- they never joined is worse than no row.
UPDATE chat_eval_jobs
   SET status      = 'unscoreable',
       claim_token = NULL,
       claim_until = NULL,
       claimed_at  = NULL,
       last_error  = left($3::text, 500),
       updated_at  = now()
 WHERE interaction_id = $1::uuid
   AND claim_token    = $2::uuid
   AND status         = 'evaluating'
RETURNING interaction_id::text AS interaction_id, status, last_error;

parameters.query:
-- fence-exempt: single-statement UPDATE. The fence IS the statement's own
-- WHERE clause, so the row is locked and the predicate re-evaluated against
-- the latest committed version by the UPDATE itself (EvalPlanQual). There is
-- no read-then-write window to widen, and adding FOR UPDATE would only take
-- the same lock twice.
-- Terminal success. The lease is released and last_error cleared, so a row that
-- previously failed does not keep a stale reason attached to a good result.
--
-- Retryable. The judge was unreachable, rate limited, or still contradicted
-- the rubric after its one correction.
--
-- Backed off by attempt number: a judge that is down stays down for minutes,
-- and retrying immediately turns a rate limit into a ban.
UPDATE chat_eval_jobs
   SET status = CASE WHEN judge_attempts >= 3 THEN 'dead_letter' ELSE 'judge_failed' END,
       claim_token     = NULL,
       claim_until     = NULL,
       claimed_at      = NULL,
       next_attempt_at = now() + (interval '5 minutes' * GREATEST(judge_attempts, 1)),
       last_error      = left($3::text, 500),
       updated_at      = now()
 WHERE interaction_id = $1::uuid
   AND claim_token    = $2::uuid
   AND status         = 'evaluating'
RETURNING interaction_id::text AS interaction_id, status, judge_attempts, last_error;

parameters.query:
-- Every judge call, with what it cost. 006 created this table; nothing has ever
-- written to it, so every cost figure this project has produced was arithmetic
-- over a sample rather than a measurement.
--
-- lease-exempt: append-only, and unique on (purpose, input_hash, prompt_version)
-- with ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING. input_hash is the hash of the exact text sent, so
-- a stale worker re-recording the same call writes a row that is either
-- identical or skipped -- there is no state here for it to corrupt. That same
-- key is also the second cost guard: a workflow re-run over an unchanged thread
-- records no new row, and the absence of that row is how a real month-over-month
-- rise is told apart from a replay.
--
-- ONE jsonb PARAMETER, not one per field: n8n splits queryReplacement on commas,
-- and a dozen scalars would shred into a dozen bogus parameters.
INSERT INTO model_calls (
  interaction_id, purpose, provider, model, prompt_version, input_hash,
  prompt_tokens, output_tokens, cached_tokens, cost_usd, priced_at_peak,
  succeeded, error)
SELECT $1::uuid,
       c->>'purpose', c->>'provider', c->>'model', c->>'prompt_version',
       c->>'input_hash',
       (c->>'prompt_tokens')::int, (c->>'output_tokens')::int,
       (c->>'cached_tokens')::int, (c->>'cost_usd')::numeric,
       (c->>'priced_at_peak')::boolean,
       coalesce((c->>'succeeded')::boolean, true), c->>'error'
FROM jsonb_array_elements($2::jsonb) AS c
WHERE c->>'input_hash' IS NOT NULL
ON CONFLICT (purpose, input_hash, prompt_version) DO NOTHING
RETURNING call_id, purpose, cost_usd;

-- One row per distinct thing the customer asked for (017).
--
-- WHY THIS EXISTS. interaction_analysis holds exactly one service, one intent
-- and one budget, so a chat where the customer asked about a package AND a visa
-- lost the second one silently -- and the agent who opened one deal instead of
-- two looked correct in every report.
--
-- FENCED, like every other durable write here. This is an UPSERT keyed on
-- (interaction_id, seq): a stale execution holding an older reading of the
-- thread would overwrite a newer one, so `lease` takes a real row lock on a LIVE
-- claim and every write below selects FROM it. An unlocked existence check
-- would not do -- it reads a snapshot and lets go, and the recovery sweep can
-- reclaim the row inside that window while this write still commits.
--
-- EVERY VALUE IS ALREADY COERCED. The worker turned dates, budgets and enum
-- labels into safe values before they got here: an unparseable date raises
-- 22007 and Postgres aborts the WHOLE statement, which would lose the four good
-- requests along with the bad one.
--
-- seq 1 IS MATCHED TO THE CRM DEAL. The primary request is the one the agent
-- logged; every later seq is unmatched until proven otherwise, and
-- v_request_reconciliation counts exactly those as opportunities nobody opened
-- a deal for.
WITH lease AS MATERIALIZED (
  SELECT j.interaction_id
  FROM chat_eval_jobs j
  WHERE j.interaction_id = $1::uuid
    AND j.claim_token    = $2::uuid
    AND j.status         = 'evaluating'
    AND j.claim_until    > now()
  FOR UPDATE
)
INSERT INTO interaction_requests (
  interaction_id, seq, service, service_raw, intent, buying_stage, destination,
  date_start, date_end, nights, travelers_total, budget_amount, budget_currency,
  outcome, evidence, evidence_valid, matched_bitrix_deal_id, prompt_version)
SELECT $1::uuid,
       (r->>'seq')::int,
       (r->>'service')::service_type,
       r->>'service_raw',
       r->>'intent',
       (r->>'buying_stage')::buying_stage,
       r->>'destination',
       (r->>'date_start')::date,
       (r->>'date_end')::date,
       (r->>'nights')::int,
       (r->>'travelers_total')::int,
       (r->>'budget_amount')::numeric,
       r->>'budget_currency',
       r->>'outcome',
       coalesce(r->'evidence', '[]'::jsonb),
       (r->>'evidence_valid')::boolean,
       CASE WHEN (r->>'seq')::int = 1 THEN $4 END,
       $5
FROM lease, jsonb_array_elements($3::jsonb) AS r
ON CONFLICT (interaction_id, seq) DO UPDATE SET
  service         = EXCLUDED.service,
  service_raw     = EXCLUDED.service_raw,
  intent          = EXCLUDED.intent,
  buying_stage    = EXCLUDED.buying_stage,
  destination     = EXCLUDED.destination,
  date_start      = EXCLUDED.date_start,
  date_end        = EXCLUDED.date_end,
  nights          = EXCLUDED.nights,
  travelers_total = EXCLUDED.travelers_total,
  budget_amount   = EXCLUDED.budget_amount,
  budget_currency = EXCLUDED.budget_currency,
  outcome         = EXCLUDED.outcome,
  evidence        = EXCLUDED.evidence,
  evidence_valid  = EXCLUDED.evidence_valid,
  prompt_version  = EXCLUDED.prompt_version
RETURNING request_id, seq, service, evidence_valid;
